summary: Iter 33 — School Notification cards now classified by semantic KIND (no TELEGRAM/WHATSAPP label) + parent quick-reply round-trip. Backend: 66/66 across all 5 messaging suites when run separately (12+10+14+16+14). Iter33 alone: 14/14. Frontend (parent): School Notifications thread shows semantic cards (Attendance Alert, Holiday Notice, School Notice) with kind icons + colored left borders; NO 'TELEGRAM'/'WHATSAPP' text label anywhere; quick-reply chips render (Acknowledged / My child is unwell / Will be there tomorrow / Got it thanks / Need more info); tap → toast 'Sent to <staff name>' fires, chip group disappears, 'You replied: <text>' chip appears beneath bubble (verified count: 13→12 qr groups, 4→5 done chips after a single click); replied state persists (previously-replied bubbles already showed 'You replied:' on first load). NOTE: a pre-existing flaky asyncio motor-loop binding makes test_iter32_system_peer_pin_mute.py::TestMirrorWsFire fail when bundled in a single pytest process with iter29/30/31; running each suite separately (as iter32 also did) is the supported regression mode and gives 66/66 green.

critical_code_review_comments: messaging.py _KIND_BY_TEMPLATE covers 13 known templates; _classify_update has best-effort partial-match fallbacks ('fee', 'attend', 'absent', 'exam', 'result', 'sick', 'holiday', 'trip') with sensible defaults to 'general'. Channel field intentionally NOT surfaced on the bubble payload (per spec) — confirmed at line 414-440 (_chat_update_to_message returns only kind/kind_label/kind_color/quick_replies/replied_at/reply_text alongside the canonical message keys).

messaging.py /system/reply route correctly: (a) validates owner via {recipient_id: user.id} in lookup → 404 for non-owner / non-existent, (b) blocks double-reply with 409, (c) resolves recipient via _resolve_reply_recipient with attendance/sick/exam → class teacher (via class_teacher_map on student.class_id + section) and fee/unknown → first school_admin, (d) reuses _upsert_conversation + tdb.messages.insert + _trim_conversation_history so the reply behaves like a normal 1-1 message, (e) marks chat_updates.replied_at + reply_text + reply_recipient_id, (f) WS-fans to both sender and recipient and optionally web-pushes if recipient is offline.

Composed message prefix '↩︎ Re: <subject> · <student name> (<uid>)\n\n<text>' — verified end-to-end via test_attendance_reply_routes_to_class_teacher; the teacher's inbox contains exactly this format.
QuickReplyIn Pydantic model has min_length=1 on both update_id and text — 422 on empty text confirmed.

Routing nit: when kind=='fee' the code still falls through to school_admin (no accounts user lookup) — the inline comment explicitly says 'accounts users aren't chat-enabled in this app'. Intentional and matches the spec ('fee → school_admin'). Same for general/unknown.

ChatPage.jsx KIND_META covers attendance/fee/exam/sick/holiday/trip/general with per-kind icon + Tailwind border color; MessageBubble shows .chat-quick-replies group + per-chip data-testid='chat-quick-reply-<msgid>-<slug>' and .chat-quick-reply-done with data-testid='chat-quick-reply-done-<msgid>' for replied state. Excellent testability.

Each capped by the existing per-(recipient_id, related_student_id) cap of 7. Several were replied via /messaging/system/reply, stamping replied_at + reply_text. The class teacher (priya) accordingly has a TEST_iter33_-prefixed 1-1 thread with several '↩︎ Re:' messages.
context_for_next_testing_agent: FIVE messaging backend test files now form the chat regression suite: test_messaging.py (12), test_iter30_messaging_v2.py (10), test_iter31_groups_updates.py (14), test_iter32_system_peer_pin_mute.py (16), test_iter33_system_replies.py (14). RUN EACH AS A SEPARATE PYTEST INVOCATION — motor binds its first-touched event loop and any test that drives async backend code in-process (TestMirrorWsFire, TestClassification, TestSystemBubblePayload, TestQuickReply) cannot share a process with another in-process async caller. iter33 uses a module-level _LOOP for this purpose. The reply endpoint requires update_id to be a chat_updates id OWNED by the caller (recipient_id == user.id); cross-owner returns 404. For attendance/sick/exam routing to class teacher, callers MUST pass context={'student_id': <real student.id>} — NOT student_uid 'STU-00001'. The mirror code copies context['student_id'] verbatim into chat_updates.related_student_id, and the resolver does tdb.students.find_one({'id': sid}). Real notification routes (e.g. /attendance/bulk) already pass student['id'] correctly. /system/reply composes '↩︎ Re: <subject> · <student name> (<uid>)\n\n<text>' — the student segment is only added when related_student_id is present. Channel field is INTENTIONALLY removed from the bubble payload; do not add it back as an assertion in any test.
rca of the issue: No product issues found. One pre-existing test-infra issue surfaces only when multiple async-backend test files are bundled in a single pytest process (motor event-loop binding). Mitigation already in place: run each suite separately, which matches how iter32 also reported its 67/67.
